content.value_statement: Vue and Nuxt projects often reimplement state, browser, sensor, timing, and utility logic. This skill maps requirements to VueUse composables and provides focused usage guidance from local references.
actual_capabilities: Maps Vue and Nuxt feature requirements to VueUse composables across state, browser, sensors, network, animation, reactivity, arrays, time, and utilities.
Distinguishes automatic, explicit-only, and external-dependency composables using the invocation table in the skill instructions.
Points to local reference files that include usage examples, options, return values, and TypeScript declarations.
Guides implementations for reactive storage, clipboard, media, keyboard, network, routing, and browser API patterns.
Helps refactor custom Vue logic into maintained VueUse composables when the replacement improves clarity.
limitations: It requires a Vue 3 or Nuxt 3 project where VueUse is available.
External integration composables may require additional packages before use.
It does not replace review of permissions, network endpoints, file access, or privacy-sensitive UI behavior.
The bundled references may not include every change from future VueUse releases.

use_cases.description: Plan Nuxt-safe usage for storage, media, clipboard, permissions, sensors, and network composables.

prompt_templates.title: Find a VueUse Function
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a Vue 3 feature that needs [describe behavior]. Which VueUse composable should I use, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use VueUse to implement [feature] in a Nuxt 3 component. Explain the composables, required dependencies, and important options.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vue logic and replace custom watchers, timers, or browser API wrappers with VueUse composables where it improves clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Composable Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Vue module for VueUse opportunities. Separate automatic choices from external integrations, explicit-only functions, and privacy-sensitive APIs.

output_examples.input: I need a Nuxt search page with debounced input and remote loading state.
output: Recommends a debounced ref or debounced function for the query input.
Uses a reactive async state or fetch composable for loading, result, and error state.
Calls out network endpoint review and cancellation behavior.

output_examples.input: I want to track whether a panel is visible and resize it responsively.
output: Recommends element visibility, size, and resize observer composables.
Notes that DOM-dependent logic should run only on the client in SSR apps.
Explains when a plain Vue ref is still enough.

output_examples.input: I need keyboard shortcuts for a Vue editor.
output: Recommends keyboard composables for explicit shortcut keys only.
Warns against capturing all typing or logging sensitive input.
Includes cleanup and passive event guidance.

best_practices: Consult the referenced VueUse document before using a composable, especially for options and return values.
Use external integration composables only when the project already has the required dependency or the user approves it.
Review privacy and permission impact before adding keyboard, clipboard, media, file, location, or notification APIs.
anti_patterns: Capturing all keyboard input when a narrow shortcut or form event would solve the problem.
Adding an external integration package only because a VueUse wrapper exists.
Replacing simple Vue primitives with obscure wrappers when the result is harder to read.

faq.question: What projects can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for Vue 3 and Nuxt 3 projects that can use VueUse composables.

faq.question: Does it install VueUse automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides selection and usage. Package installation should follow the user and project setup.

faq.question: How does it choose a composable?
faq.answer: It matches the requested behavior to the function table, then checks the local reference for usage details.

faq.question: Can it use external VueUse integrations?
faq.answer: Yes, but only when the needed dependency is already present or the user agrees that it should be added.

faq.question: Does it cover browser permission concerns?
faq.answer: It can flag relevant concerns, but developers must still review user consent, privacy, and browser support.

faq.question: Can it replace custom code during refactors?
faq.answer: Yes. It is useful for replacing repeated reactive utilities when VueUse makes the implementation clearer.
